results.title: How Much Blackwell Actually Exists? | TheAI Blog
highlights:
Now measure it. On getdeploying's B300 index (Aug 18): 23 providers list B300 at all — fewer than B200 (27), H200 (37), or H100 (53). Of those 23, 15 publish an on-demand price and only 10 show live stock. B300 is the thinnest supply segment in the market. On one of the largest B2B cluster marketplaces, we counted 34 public B300 listings this week: every EU listing carries 5-year terms only with Feb 2027+ delivery; US listings cluster at 36–60 months; listings with any term under 12 months: two. Earliest available date on the entire board: October 8 — one 8-node lot.

...

First, the price signal itself, decomposed — with one honesty note up front: we lack a per-provider November snapshot, so the full 57 points can't be attributed one by one. But from March onward, where archive panels exist, the documented driver is same-provider repricing: Enverge went $5.00→$7.50, Verda $5.74→$7.50, Nebius's own price list moved B300 from $6.10 to $7.85 between May and July — while cheap new entrants roughly offset the hyperscaler listings that joined, leaving index composition a minor term. B200 tells the same story: of twelve providers listed since March, eight raised prices and none cut; Lambda's cluster pricing nearly doubled. One honest caveat in the other direction: the entire repricing wave happened between March and early July — like-for-like prices have been flat for the past six weeks. The market ratcheted up, then held.

The rest of the evidence is behavioral: SemiAnalysis reported in April that on-demand capacity was sold out across all GPU types and new Blackwell deployments were quoting into mid-2026 and beyond; buyers are signing 2027 delivery at 2026 prices; marketplace boards price future delivery with no discount for the wait. H100 one-year contracts — three-year-old silicon — bottomed at $1.70 in October 2025 and have since rebounded 40% as agent workloads ate every idle card; the full curve gets its own section below. When last-generation prices are "melting up" (Latent.Space's phrase), the current generation doesn't crash.

...

But the second half of the curve is the part nobody quotes: from the October 2025 bottom, H100 contract prices rebounded 40% by March 2026, on-demand sold out again, and the erosion stopped well above zero — because inference and agent workloads found the floor. Silicon depreciates; it doesn't evaporate. The honest model for Blackwell: hold through the current shortage window (prices, lead times, sold-out boards all point at 6–12+ more months), erode as Rubin volume actually lands and 2025's multi-year contracts start expiring (2027 onward), then find a workload floor rather than a cliff.

results.title: %7 arttı token harcaması, B200 kirası ilk kez düştü - TokenPost
highlights:
Ağustos ayında yapay zeka modeli çağrılarına olan talep artmaya devam etti, ancak 'token' harcamasındaki artış kullanım artışının çok gerisinde kaldı. Nvidia(NVDA)'nın en yeni GPU'su B200'ün kiralama fiyatı ise Eylül 2025'teki endeks lansmanından bu yana ilk kez aylık bazda geriledi.

TechFlow, 28'inde (yerel saatte) JPMorgan(JPM)'ın Ağustos raporuna dayanarak, OpenRouter platformundaki token kullanımının bir önceki aya göre yüzde 47, geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre ise 28 kat arttığını aktardı. Aynı dönemde token harcaması ise aylık bazda yüzde 7, yıllık bazda 12 kat yükseldi.

...

GPU kiralama piyasasında nesiller arasında farklı bir tablo ortaya çıktı. A100 kirası saatte 1,65 dolarda yatay seyretti. H100 ise saatte 2,73 dolara yükselerek aylık bazda yüzde 1,2 toparlandı.

Buna karşılık B200, saatte 5,63 dolara gerileyerek aylık bazda yüzde 1,5 düştü. JPMorgan, B200 fiyatındaki bu gerilemenin Eylül 2025'teki endeks lansmanından bu yana ilk aylık düşüş olduğunu belirtti. En yeni nesil GPU arzındaki değişimin fiyatlara yansımaya başladığı yorumu yapılabilir.

Yalnızca B200 fiyatındaki düşüşe bakarak yapay zeka hesaplama talebinde bir yavaşlama olduğunu söylemek güç. H100 kirasındaki toparlanma, bir önceki nesil GPU'lara yönelik talebin hâlâ canlı olduğunu gösteriyor. A100, H100 ve B200 fiyatlarının aynı yönde hareket etmemesi, yapay zeka altyapı maliyetinin tek bir göstergeyle özetlenemeyeceğine işaret ediyor.

...

Bu veriler, yapay zeka altyapı piyasasındaki maliyet yapısının yalnızca GPU kira fiyatlarıyla açıklanamayacağını gösteriyor. Token kullanımı, model birim fiyatı, GPU kirası ile DRAM ve NAND spot fiyatları birbirinden farklı hızlarda hareket ediyor. Bir sonraki aylık verilerde, B200 fiyatındaki düşüşün arz artışına bağlı geçici bir düzeltme mi yoksa GPU nesilleri arasında kalıcı bir fiyat yeniden yapılanmasının başlangıcı mı olduğu netleşecek.

results.title: packet.ai vs Crusoe: GPU Cloud Comparison 2026 | packet.ai
highlights:
packet.ai team Aug 27, 2026 6 min read

...

B200 from $4.25/hr, RTX 4090 from $0.39/hr. Hourly, no contract.

Crusoe started by putting GPUs next to flared natural gas and has grown into one of the largest neoclouds by contracted power, with multi-gigawatt data centre projects. It sells H100, H200, A100 and AMD MI300X on demand, with Blackwell available through sales, and pitches itself on cost and sustainability at scale.

packet.ai does not build power plants. It squeezes more useful work out of each GPU through scheduling and sells the result hourly. This comparison looks at the on-demand rate cards, which overlap on the A100 80GB, and at the very different ways each company gets to a low number.

...

### What Crusoe offers

Crusoe's published on-demand per-GPU rates in August 2026: HGX H100 $3.90/hr, HGX H200 $4.29/hr, A100 80GB SXM $2.30/hr, AMD MI300X $3.45/hr, L40S about $1.50/hr. B200, GB200 NVL72 and MI355X are quoted by sales. Egress is free and committed-use discounts are sales-quoted.

- Energy-first infrastructure: data centres sited at stranded or renewable power
- Managed Kubernetes and Slurm, InfiniBand clusters, enterprise support
- Blackwell on-demand pricing not published; contact sales
- No consumer or workstation GPUs

...

Crusoe's cost story starts upstream, at the power source. packet.ai's starts at the GPU itself: the scheduler keeps a card doing useful work a higher share of the time, and that recovered utilisation is passed back as a lower published rate. On the one card both list, the A100 80GB, that shows up directly: $0.89/hr Dynamic on packet.ai against $2.30/hr on Crusoe, a 61% gap.

The bigger difference is what happens above Ampere. Crusoe's B200 is not on its rate card at all, it is quoted through sales. packet.ai publishes a B200 rate you can deploy against today.

- Dynamic: scheduler-enforced multi-tenant, published rate, no sales call. B200 starting at $4.25/hr, RTX 6000 Pro at $0.76/hr, both of which Crusoe does not list on-demand.
- Dedicated: a whole card, single-tenant, 99% SLA. RTX 4090 at $0.39/hr, B200 at $7.99/hr (also 2×, 3× and 8× nodes). The A100 80GB ($0.89/hr) is Dynamic only; the L40S is coming soon.

What Crusoe has that packet.ai does not: published Hopper rates (H100 $3.90/hr, H200 $4.29/hr) that packet.ai's notify-list H100/H200 cannot yet match, AMD MI300X, and a genuine energy-sourcing story for buyers with sustainability requirements written into procurement. If you need Hopper today or a contracted power narrative, Crusoe has both. If you need Blackwell on demand without a sales conversation, packet.ai does.

Billing is hourly; the one monthly plan is 2× B200 Dedicated at $11,665.40/mo. There are no platform fees and no ingress charges; egress is $0.04/GB. Up to 2 TB of local NVMe per node is included. Dynamic instances are SSH-ready in under five minutes, Dedicated in five to ten. Capacity is live in the US (California, Virginia, Texas, Oregon) and Europe (Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Paris, London, Dublin). H100 SXM, H200 and RTX 5090 are on the notify list.

...

### On-demand rate cards

results.title: 2026 GPU Neocloud选型指南：公开定价、签约电力与Kubernetes验证
highlights:
Neocloud 是最近几年兴起的一类云服务商，典型特征就是成立之初就把 GPU 训练和推理当作核心业务，而不是“计算实例里顺带支持 GPU”。他们通常： 

- 提供大量的 H100、H200、A100 甚至 Blackwell 系列 GPU 实例； 
- 深度集成 Kubernetes、Slurm 等调度平台； 
- 在数据中心网络层面为 GPU 集群设计 RDMA 和 InfiniBand； 
- 面向 AI Infra、模型微调、推理服务提供更灵活的计费方式。 

#### 1.2 为什么“公开定价”不能只看标价 

 很多 Neocloud 官网会直接列出按需价格，例如某厂商的 8 卡 H100 实例可能是每小时 20 多美元。但真实项目里，你很少会真的用“按需价”跑满几个月。更常见的是： 

- 预留实例（Reserved）：签年度合同，价格比按需低 30% 到 50%； 
- 抢注模式（Spot/Auction）：用竞价方式拿闲置算力，适合容错水平较高的训练任务； 
- 专用租约（Dedicated）：整机柜甚至整机房独占，可以定制网络和存储。 

 只看按需标价会明显低估长期项目成本，也容易忽视合同期内的运维成本。

...

#### 2.1 硬件规格和互联拓扑 

 需要关注的点： 

- GPU 型号：H100、H200、A100、L40S、B200 等； 
- 单实例 GPU 数量：常见是 1 卡、4 卡、8 卡； 
- GPU 互联方式：NVLink、NVSwitch、InfiniBand 或 RoCE； 
- 显存大小：H100 有 80GB，H200 是 141GB，未来 Blackwell 可能更高； 
- 本地盘类型：NVMe 还是传统 SSD，容量和 IOPS 如何。

...

#### 2.2 定价模型 

 不要只比较“每小时价格”，还要看： 

- 最小计费单位：按秒、按小时，还是按天； 
- 是否有预付费用； 
- 预留实例和即用实例的价格差； 
- 是否包含存储和网络流量； 
- 是否提供竞价/Spot 实例； 
- 停机时间怎么计费，例如节点维护是否免单。

...

```
# 文件路径：gpu_pricing_model.py
# 功能：根据按需价和预留折扣，估算一个月GPU资源总成本

...

PROVIDERS = {
    "provider_a": {
        "gpu_type": "H100 80G",
        "on_demand_per_hour": 2.49,       # 单卡每小时价格，单位：美元
        "reserved_discount": 0.4,          # 预留实例折扣，0.4表示打六折
        "min_reserved_months": 12,
        "power_commit_required": False,
        "setup_fee": 500,                  # 一次性配置费
    },
    "provider_b": {
        "gpu_type": "H100 80G",
        "on_demand_per_hour": 2.19,
        "reserved_discount": 0.45,
        "min_reserved_months": 6,
        "power_commit_required": True,
        "setup_fee": 2000,
    },
    "provider_c": {
        "gpu_type": "H200 141G",
        "on_demand_per_hour": 3.99,
        "reserved_discount": 0.35,
        "min_reserved_months": 12,
        "power_commit_required": True,
        "setup_fee": 0,
    },
}

...

不同 GPU 型号之间不能直接比较每小时的绝对价格。比如 H100 80G 和 H200 141G，显存差异巨大，但价格差距可能早就超过显存带来的训练收益。建议用“每 TFLOPS/小时”或“每 token/秒”作为度量，再结合业务场景看性价比。

results.title: [SMM Analysis] Computing Power Rental Chaos on the Rise: H200 Hyped to 137,000, 4090 Inflated by 18% - Shanghai Metals Market (SMM)
highlights:
SMM learned from channel sources that amid the price war, hidden chaos in compute leasing is surfacing: smaller providers are taking orders below cost while intermediaries bid prices above mainstream levels. For one batch of 128 H200 units, the owner quoted 116,000–117,000 yuan per unit/month (8-GPU system, 4–5-year contract), but intermediaries resold at 137,000 — an 18% markup. The 4090 anchor was 7,200 yuan per unit/month; after multiple flips, end-user quotes hit 8,500, also up ~18%.

...

The 2026 computing power leasing price war saw bidding centers continuously shift downward — according to domestic media reports, small and medium service providers took orders below cost, accelerating industry reshuffle; yet during this chaotic period, the intermediary layer grew bolder in quoting above mainstream transaction prices: For the same batch of 128 H200 resources, the cargo owner directly quoted 116,000-117,000 yuan/unit/month (on an 8-card complete machine basis, 4-5 year long-term contract), and intermediaries resold at 137,000 yuan/unit/month — a one-hand premium of about 18%; the 4090 market transaction anchor point stood at about 7,200 yuan/unit/month, and after multiple handovers, end-user asking prices reached 8,500 yuan (a case of 45 units in a city in east China), artificially inflated by about 18%. What fell was asset prices, what rose was information gap arbitrage — behind low prices lurked hidden costs of fake goods, intermediary stacking, and contract idling. SMM believes that the price war amplified information asymmetry, and the essence of the chaos was the three-no low prices of "no delivery capability + no contract closure

One-year H100 rental pricing rose from about $1.70 per GPU-hour in October 2025 to about $2.35 per GPU-hour in March 2026. Cross-provider on-demand median pricing rose from roughly $2.00 per GPU-hour in October 2025 to $2.70 in June 2026. highlights:
- GPU cloud pricing meters per GPU-hour, with separate line items for data egress and storage that quietly inflate the bill.
- On-demand H100 rentals run roughly $2.99 to $10.98 per GPU-hour as of September 2026, depending on provider. Reserved and spot cost less but trade flexibility.
- The bill is large, spiky, and in US dollars, so a card that gets declined on a spike or adds FX is a real operational risk.

...

| Mode | What it is | Trade-off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On-demand | Pay-as-you-go per GPU-hour, no commitment, start and stop anytime. | Highest rate per hour, but full flexibility and nothing owed when idle. |
| Reserved / committed | Commit to a term or a fixed amount of capacity in exchange for a lower rate. | Cheaper per hour, but you pay for the commitment whether you use it or not. |
| Spot | Bid on the provider's spare capacity at a steep discount. | Cheapest, but the provider can reclaim it with little notice, so it fits interruptible jobs only.

## How much does an H100 cost per hour?

As of September 2026, on-demand NVIDIA H100 rentals run roughly $2.99 to $10.98 per GPU-hour. The lower end tends to sit at specialist GPU clouds, and the higher end at the large hyperscalers. Some providers advertise even lower spot rates for interruptible capacity. Prices vary by provider, region, and contract, and they move fast, so treat any number as a snapshot and re-check a live source before you budget. See the Thunder Compute H100 pricing breakdown for a current comparison.
